{
  "summary": "Optimizes primitive serialization and serialized size calculation across Bitcoin Core's stream, crypto, and serialization primitives. It adds single-byte write and read overloads using fixed-extent spans (std::span<..., 1>) across AutoFile, DataStream, VectorWriter, and SHA-256 contexts to bypass general buffer allocations and memcpy calls. In addition, it consolidates primitive integer serialization using C++20 concepts and if constexpr, allowing SizeComputer to advance byte offsets directly without performing endianness conversions.",
  "problem": "Generic serialization routines impose small per-element overheads that accumulate during high-volume operations like block serialization and Initial Block Download (IBD). Single-byte writes (e.g. booleans, VarInt prefix bytes, and int8 types) invoke general stream buffering or memcpy, while SizeComputer pointlessly computes endian transformations when only the byte length matters.",
  "evidence": [
    "Author's nanobench results report SerializeBlock latency improving from ~195 µs to ~174 µs on AppleClang and from ~867 µs to ~615 µs on GCC 13, with SizeComputerBlock dropping from ~12.0 µs to ~10.2 µs on AppleClang and ~30.9 µs to ~25.6 µs on GCC.",
    "Author's 3-run hyperfine IBD benchmark to block height 880,000 reports bitcoind running '1.02 ± 0.02 times faster' (mean wall time reduced from 33,647s to 33,062s)."
  ],

The PR adds fixed-extent single-byte write and read methods to streams and hashers, and short-circuits SizeComputer passes in serialize.h. result.summary: Optimizes primitive serialization and serialized size calculation across Bitcoin Core's stream, crypto, and serialization primitives. It adds single-byte write and read overloads using fixed-extent spans (std::span<..., 1>) across AutoFile, DataStream, VectorWriter, and SHA-256 contexts to bypass general buffer allocations and memcpy calls. In addition, it consolidates primitive integer serialization using C++20 concepts and if constexpr, allowing SizeComputer to advance byte offsets directly without performing endianness conversions.
result.problem: Generic serialization routines impose small per-element overheads that accumulate during high-volume operations like block serialization and Initial Block Download (IBD). Single-byte writes (e.g. booleans, VarInt prefix bytes, and int8 types) invoke general stream buffering or memcpy, while SizeComputer pointlessly computes endian transformations when only the byte length matters.
evidence: Author's nanobench results report SerializeBlock latency improving from ~195 µs to ~174 µs on AppleClang and from ~867 µs to ~615 µs on GCC 13, with SizeComputerBlock dropping from ~12.0 µs to ~10.2 µs on AppleClang and ~30.9 µs to ~25.6 µs on GCC.
Author's 3-run hyperfine IBD benchmark to block height 880,000 reports bitcoind running '1.02 ± 0.02 times faster' (mean wall time reduced from 33,647s to 33,062s).
result.scope_notes: Touches core serialization logic in serialize.h, stream interfaces in streams.{h,cpp}, and cryptographic hash wrappers in sha256.{h,cpp} and hash.h, alongside new microbenchmarks in checkblock.cpp.
result.card: Specializes single-byte stream operations and optimizes SizeComputer paths across serialization primitives. Currently, single-byte serialization invokes generic buffer checks and memcpy operations, and SizeComputer executes unnecessary endianness conversions when calculating sizes. The PR adds fixed-extent single-byte write and read methods to streams and hashers, and short-circuits SizeComputer passes in serialize.h. Microbenchmarks from the author indicate an 11% to 29% reduction in block serialization time and a ~2% speedup in full IBD to height 880,000.
